summary: The contract is one fixed-width scalar query, so constant output work matches the closed-form upper bound and runtime tiers cannot measure a smaller asymptotic class.

optimality.argument: Every correct implementation must produce one integer answer for the scalar query. Evaluating 1 + 2n(n - 1) uses a fixed number of arithmetic operations independent of n, matching that unavoidable constant work.

replacement_checks.evidence: Producing the required integer result for the fixed-arity query requires at least one operation.
The reference evaluates one subtraction, two multiplications, one addition, and one return, with no input-dependent iteration or storage.

Authored cases cover the first layers, odd and power-of-ten minute counts, and the 64-bit maximum result; an independent cumulative-layer recurrence also matched the formula for every legal n from 1 through 100000.
